chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Isma'il ibn Marrar from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said:
Whoever washes a dead believer and fulfills the trust in it, he is forgiven. It was said: And how does he fulfill the trust in it? He said: He does not inform others about what he sees.

key_terms.أمانة: amanah - trust, the duty of confidentiality
key_terms.غسل: ghusl - ritual washing of the deceased

ai.seo_question: What is the trust (amanah) that must be kept when washing a deceased person in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the ethical obligation of maintaining confidentiality when performing the funeral washing (ghusl al-mayyit). The concept of 'amanah' (trust) here refers to concealing any defects or conditions observed on the deceased's body, as the washer is in a position of sacred trust. The reward for upholding this trust is complete forgiveness, underscoring the gravity Islam places on protecting human dignity even after death.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. Ziyad b. Ja`far al-Hamadani (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim from Isma`il b. Marrar from Yunus b. `Abd al-Rahman from `Abdullah b. Sinan from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as). He said:
Whoever washes a dead believer and fulfills his trust, he is forgiven. It was said: How does he fulfill his trust? He said: He does not inform others about what he saw.
